name: Papal Inquisition Established in Languedoc
summary: Following the Albigensian Crusade (1209–1229), Pope Gregory IX in 1233 appointed Dominican friars as permanent inquisitors in Languedoc to investigate surviving Catharism. The Papal Inquisition developed systematic procedures: denunciation, interrogation, use of torture (authorized 1252), and graduated penalties from penance to burning. The fall of Montségur in 1244, where 200 Cathars were burned, effectively ended organized Catharism.
outcomes: Pope Gregory IX appoints Dominican inquisitors

_quarry.structural_significance: Established the institutional inquisition as a permanent instrument of the church; its procedures, particularly the use of torture and anonymous denunciation, became the template for later inquisitions.
